doc.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022

chapter: Vegas groups and Spokane solo years
title: The Plantation and the drummer-owner who seated customers
summary: At The Plantation with organist Tony Pasco and owner Perry Williams on drums, who stopped to seat guests mid-song.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well it was tough. I’d talk to the kids, the other three kids were old enough to talk to me and my old lady and my youngest son was just a baby at the time. It was very difficult. And then this manager, this John Powell, you know at least now I was making $300 a week, I could send, you know $250 home through Western Union so she could pay the rent and buy some food. And it was really just stretching it out. And then John Powell said, “Hey, you’re packing the room, I’m going to ask for more money.” And then he came to me and said, “Rocky said he can’t afford to pay any more money so I got a club across town you can work called The Plantation and the guy likes you, he’s been in to see you. Perry Williams is his name.” I said great. So I went to the club, he says, over there you’re going to have a band behind you. I said, “Whoa, I’m back in show biz.” So I went there and the band consisted of an organ player named Tony Pasco. No matter what he played it sounded like a roller rink, you know that sound. So we rehearsed a little bit with

Tony and the rest of the band was a drummer. So it was an organ and drums, and the drummer was the owner of the club, Perry Williams, who played drums once in a while. So opening night, as bad as it was, it was still better than where I was and so I was thanking God for that and I went out and I was singing some song to open, “The Lady is a Tramp” or something, to open the show. And halfway through the drums stopped. Well you know I’m in show business, I’m not going to turn around and say what happened to the drummer — so I just keep singing. Out of the corner of my eye I see my drummer, who is the club owner, walking down the aisle in front, picks up to menus “party of two” he seated people. My drummer was seating people during the show. It was like — anyway —
You know somehow that seems like if I can get through this man, I can do pretty much anything.
